# Hermes Agent: Onboarding & Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Welcome to **Hermes Agent**! This guide covers core architecture, platform setup, model configurations, plugin development, gateway integrations, and solutions to known issues.

---

## 1. Installation, Platform & Environment Support

### Supported Platforms
- **Linux & macOS**: Supported natively via the standard installer (`curl -fsSL ... | bash`).
- **Windows**: Windows 10/11 is a **Tier 1 supported platform** via native PowerShell (`install.ps1`). WSL2 is not required except for POSIX PTY support in the Web Dashboard embedded terminal.
- **Docker & NAS**: Official multi-arch Docker images (`nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest`) support `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` (Apple Silicon, Raspberry Pi; shipped in v2026.4.13). For NAS platforms (UGOS Pro, Synology, unRAID) with bind-mount permission issues, pass `PUID` and `PGID` (or `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID`) environment variables (fixed in v2026.6.5).
- **Android / Termux**: Supported out of the box (v2026.7.1). `install.sh` detects Termux, sets `ANDROID_API_LEVEL`, installs `termux-all` dependencies, and uses a writable `TMPDIR`.

### Why is `hermes update` slow on Node.js dependencies?
The update process installs packages like Camofox, which silently downloads browser binaries during the postinstall phase without progress output.

---

## 2. Models, Providers & API Configuration

### How do I configure local models (Ollama, LocalAI)?
- **Preventing Auto-Routing**: If environment variables like `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` exist, `provider: auto` might route requests remotely. Explicitly set:
  ```yaml
  model:
    default: ollama/<model-name>
    provider: custom
    base_url: http://localhost:11434/v1
  fallback_providers: []
  ```
- **Performance Optimization for Small Models (4B–9B)**: Hermes passes the full tool schema (~45 tools) on each turn. For smaller models:
  - Disable unneeded tools with `hermes tools`.
  - Use faster quantization or larger models (32B+) for tool-heavy workflows.
  - Set `terminal.backend: local` to eliminate container overhead.
- **Vision Support**: Enable vision payloads on custom/Ollama endpoints by setting `supports_vision: true` in your model configuration.
- **Token Usage Tracking**: Hermes automatically passes `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}` on streaming OpenAI-compatible calls so `/usage` reports accurate token counts.

### Provider Integration & Known Provider Issues
- **Ollama Cloud**: Shipped in v2026.5.28 (v0.15.0), the built-in `ollama-cloud` provider routes requests to the OpenAI-compatible `https://ollama.com/v1` endpoint, fixing 404 errors caused by legacy `/api` routes. Run `hermes update` if encountering 404s.
- **Azure AI Foundry**: Set `provider: azure-foundry` or run `hermes setup`. Hermes auto-detects `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL`.
- **Anthropic / Claude Code**: API keys bill under standard API usage. To use your Claude Pro/Max subscription allowance, authenticate via OAuth.
- **Google Gemini**: Legacy CLI OAuth providers (`google-gemini-cli`, `google-antigravity`) were removed because Google blocks third-party OAuth flows. Authenticate using `GOOGLE_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY` (Google AI Studio) or Vertex AI.
- **DeepSeek V4 Model Normalization**: If unexpected API charges occur when configuring `deepseek-v4-flash`, ensure model normalization in `hermes_cli/model_normalize.py` is updated; earlier versions erroneously normalized `deepseek-v4-flash` to `deepseek-chat` (which upstream mapped to the pricier `deepseek-v4-pro`).
- **Open WebUI Tool Progress**: In v2026.4.8+, a bug where `_on_tool_progress` signature mismatch caused swallowed `TypeError` exceptions (resulting in missing tool progress SSE events in Open WebUI) was resolved.

### Does Hermes support automatic "smart model routing"?
**No.** Automatic complexity-based model routing (e.g., routing short turns to cheap models) was removed by maintainer design policy (`delegation-model-routing`). Hermes retains the session's primary model. For multi-model setups, configure subagents via `delegation.provider`/`delegation.model` or manually switch models with `/model <name>`.

---

## 3. Agent Core, Memory & Context Management

### Difference between `SOUL.md`, `USER.md`, and `MEMORY.md`
- **`SOUL.md`**: Defines the agent's core identity, persona, and system prompt. (Note: Early installer builds had an empty comment template; v2026.7.1 seeds a complete default persona).
- **`USER.md`**: Stores persistent user identity, preferences, and profile data (modified when tools target `target="user"`).
- **`MEMORY.md`**: Stores general cross-conversation memories, facts, and context.

### Memory Plugins & Honcho Support
- **Memory Provider Architecture**: In-tree additions to `plugins/memory/` are closed. External memory backends should be built as standalone plugins implementing the `MemoryProvider` ABC placed in `~/.hermes/plugins/`.
- **Local Honcho Server**: Fixed in v2026.3.30 (v0.4.0+), local Honcho instances (`localhost` / `127.0.0.1`) no longer fail with "Invalid API key" because Hermes auto-injects a `"local"` key placeholder when connecting to local base URLs.

### Context Management & Execution Limits
- **Context Management**: Hermes uses `ContextCompressor` (and a pluggable `ContextEngine` ABC, v2026.4.13) to prune and deduplicate tool outputs while preserving recent context.
- **Turn Limits**: Defaults to `agent.max_turns: 90` (overridable via `hermes chat --max-turns <N>`).
- **Autonomous Tasks**: For multi-turn workflows, `/goal` runs persistent goal execution loops across turns. If iteration limits pause execution, continue with `/goal resume`.

---

## 4. Tools, Skills & Observability

### Custom Tools and Plugins
Do not modify core agent files directly. Build plugins in `~/.hermes/plugins/<name>` using `ctx.register_tool(...)`, ensure the tools belong to an enabled toolset, and activate them with:
```bash
hermes plugins enable <name>
```

### Tracking Tool & Skill Usage
- Execution counts and timestamps are automatically recorded in `~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json`.
- Inspect metrics and top loaded skills by running `/insights` in chat or `hermes insights` in the CLI.
- For full observability traces (tool inputs/outputs, nested spans), enable Langfuse via `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse`.

### MCP Media Handling
MCP tool base64 `ImageContent` is cached and formatted as `MEDIA:<path>` tags (shipped in v2026.5.7), allowing gateway platforms to deliver images natively.

---

## 5. Gateway, Messaging & Web Interface

### Web Dashboard
Launch the web UI by running:
```bash
hermes dashboard
```
This opens the browser interface at `http://127.0.0.1:9119` with an embedded chat TUI.

### Gateway Setup & User Authorization
Configure messaging platforms using the interactive setup wizard:
```bash
hermes gateway setup
```
- **Telegram Authorization**: If getting "Unauthorized user", configure your Telegram user ID under `allow_from` (which sets `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS`):
  ```yaml
  telegram:
    allow_from: "123456789"
  ```
  *(Note: `allowed_chats` only restricts group chat IDs, not DMs).* Alternatively, approve incoming pairing codes via `hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>`, or set `telegram.allow_all: true`.
- **Session Reset Handling**: Fixed in v2026.5.7 (`f1e029251`), gateway restarts and interruptions set `resume_pending`, preserving session IDs and transcripts instead of wiping conversation histories. Automatic resets default to `mode: none`.
- **File & Media Delivery**: Inbound files (`.py`, `.txt`, etc.) uploaded to Discord/Telegram are injected into the context prompt (v2026.7.1). Outbound files are delivered natively via email (SMTP attachments), Matrix (`m.file`), Telegram media, and DingTalk Markdown (`![image](url)`).
- **Multi-Account & Per-Channel Personas**:
  - **Personas**: Define channel-specific system prompts using `channel_prompts` (Discord, Telegram, Slack, Mattermost).
  - **Multiplexed Gateway**: Hermes supports running multiple platform accounts (e.g., distinct WeChat/Weixin or Telegram bots) concurrently under isolated profile scopes.
  - **Subagent Delegation**: The `delegate_task` tool coordinates concurrent child agent instances.

---

## 6. Security & Support

### Reporting Vulnerabilities
Report security vulnerabilities privately via **GitHub Security Advisories** or email **security@nousresearch.com** following `SECURITY.md`. Do not open public GitHub issues for vulnerabilities.
